facts.statement: Caipirasuchus is an extinct genus of sphagesaurid notosuchians.
facts.quote: taxon: Caipirasuchus

facts.statement: The genus Caipirasuchus was first described by Iori and Carvalho in 2011.
facts.quote: authority: Iori & Carvalho, 2011

facts.statement: Fossils of Caipirasuchus date to the Late Cretaceous period.
facts.quote: fossil_range: Late Cretaceous,

facts.statement: Caipirasuchus fossils have been found in northern São Paulo State and western Minas Gerais State in southeastern Brazil.
facts.quote: known from the Late Cretaceous of northern São Paulo State and western Minas Gerais State, southeastern Brazil

facts.statement: The type species C. paulistanus was named in 2011.
facts.quote: The type species, C. paulistanus, was named in 2011.

facts.statement: The species C. montealtensis was moved to the genus Caipirasuchus in 2013, having originally been named as Sphagesaurus montealtensis in 2008.
facts.quote: A second species, C. montealtensis, was referred to Caipirasuchus in 2013 after having been named in 2008 as a species of Sphagesaurus.

facts.statement: The species C. stenognathus was described in 2014.
facts.quote: A third species, C. stenognathus, was described in 2014.

facts.statement: The species C. mineirus was described in 2018.
facts.quote: A fourth species, C. mineirus, was described in 2018.

facts.statement: The species C. attenboroughi was named in 2021 to honor the naturalist David Attenborough.
facts.quote: A fifth species, C. attenboroughi, was named in 2021 in honour of David Attenborough

facts.statement: The species C. catanduvensis was described in 2024 and features a distinct chamber linked to airways that may have been used for vocalization.
facts.quote: a sixth species, C. catanduvensis, was described in 2024, with a distinct chamber associated with the airways, possibly used in vocalization.

facts.statement: The name Caipirasuchus combines the Tupi word 'Caipira' for traditional São Paulo inhabitants and the Greek word 'souchus' meaning crocodile.
facts.quote: The generic name is derived from Tupi word Caipira which refers to the traditional inhabitants of interior of São Paulo, covering almost all of the Bauru Basin, and Greek souchus meaning "crocodile".

facts.statement: The holotype specimen of C. paulistanus was found on the São Francisco Farm in Monte Alto County, northern São Paulo.
facts.quote: It was found on the São Francisco Farm, in Homem de Mello, the rural area of Monte Alto County of northern São Paulo.

facts.statement: The holotype was collected from the Adamantina Formation of the Bauru Basin, dating to the Turonian and Santonian stages of the Late Cretaceous.
facts.quote: It was collected from the Adamantina Formation of the Bauru Basin, which dates to the Turonian and Santonian stages of the Late Cretaceous.

facts.statement: Specimens of C. catanduvensis were discovered in the municipality of Catanduva, northern São Paulo, from the Adamantina Formation.
facts.quote: It was discovered in the municipality of Catanduva, northern São Paulo, from the Adamantina Formation.

facts.statement: The holotype of C. paulistanus consists of an almost complete skull, mandible with only three missing teeth, and partial postcranium from one individual.
facts.quote: MPMA 67-0001/00, an almost complete and undeformed skull and mandible with teeth (only three teeth are missing) and partial postcranium from a single individual.

facts.statement: The specimen reassigned to C. montealtensis includes a nearly complete cranium, mandible, and posterior post-cranium.
facts.quote: MPMA 68-0003/12 consists of a nearly complete cranium and mandible, and a posterior portion of the post-cranium.

facts.statement: C. paulistanus possesses approximately ten unique characteristics known as autapomorphies.
facts.quote: C. paulistanus has about ten autapomorphies or unique characteristics.

facts.statement: In C. paulistanus, the external nostril opening is bordered solely by the premaxillae bones.
facts.quote: The external naris (the nostril opening in the skull) is bordered only by the premaxillae bones.

facts.statement: Each premaxilla in C. paulistanus contains four teeth.
facts.quote: Each premaxilla has four teeth set into it.

facts.statement: C. paulistanus has a gap called a diastema in its premaxillary tooth row and another between the premaxillary and maxillary teeth.
facts.quote: There is a gap called a diastema in the premaxillary tooth row, and a diastema in between the premaxillary and maxillary teeth.

facts.statement: The lower jaw of C. paulistanus has ten teeth on each side separated by two gaps.
facts.quote: The dentary bone of the lower jaw has ten teeth on either side, with two diastemata separating them.

facts.statement: The front teeth of C. paulistanus were adapted for capturing food, while the back teeth were adapted for processing it.
facts.quote: The forward-most teeth are suited for capturing food, while the back teeth are adapted for food processing.

facts.statement: Caipirasuchus is known from a complete skull and mandible recovered from the Adamantina Formation of the Bauru Basin, dating from the Turonian to Santonian stages of the Late Cretaceous.
facts.quote: Es conocido a partir de un cráneo completo y una mandíbula recuperados en la Formación Adamantina de la cuenca Bauru, que data de las épocas del Turoniense al Santoniense de finales del Cretácico.

facts.statement: The species C. attenboroughi was described in 2021 based on remains from the Aptian-Campanian strata of the Santo Anastácio Formation.
facts.quote: La especie C. attenboroughi fue descrita en 2021 por Bronzati, Ferreira, Martins, Lopes-Queiroz, Langer, Montefeltro y Vitor-Ruiz con base en restos procedentes de estratos de la Formación Santo Anastácio (Aptiense-Campaniense)

facts.statement: The species C. catanduvensis was described in 2024 based on Late Cretaceous fossils from the Adamantina Formation.
facts.quote: Por su parte C. catanduvensis fue descrita en 2024 por Iori, Ghilardi, Fernandes y Dias, basándose en restos fósiles del Cretácico superior procedentes de la Formación Adamantina.

facts.statement: Caipirasuchus had approximately ten unique characteristics or autapomorphies.
facts.quote: Caipirasuchus tenía cerca de diez autapomorfias o características únicas.

facts.statement: Caipirasuchus lived between 93.9 and 66 million years ago, from the Turonian to the Maastrichtian.
facts.quote: Time range: Turonian to Maastrichtian (93.9 to 66 million years ago)

facts.statement: Caipirasuchus belongs to the parent group Caipirasuchinae.
facts.quote: Parent group: Caipirasuchinae

facts.statement: Caipirasuchus is classified within the family Sphagesauridae.
facts.quote: Family: Sphagesauridae
